# Results

## ICILS

### Pooled Model

*Figure 1: ICILS global CFA model*

![](images/icils_model.png)

The ICILS initial model shown a good fit ($\chi^2$ = 5145.041; p \< .001; CFI = .97; TLI = .963; RMSEA = .031). The only metric of poor fit was a significant $\chi^2$, but given the large sample size any small difference in the covariance matrix would be significant. The loadings were medium to high for both factors, scoring between .6 and .84, and therefore, explaining among 36% and 71% of the items variance (r²). The inter-factor correlation was large, at .55. Even if highly correlated, we can identify a general and specialized dimension for digital self-eficacy in the ICILS global model, consistently with the study IRT validations and the specialized literature. The fiability and Average Variace Extracted (AVE) for both factors was above set tresholds (for General DSE: $\omega$ = .91; for Specialized DSE: $\omega$ = .8; AVE = .61).

### Invariance analysis

![](images/invariance_table_icils.png)

Regarding MGCFA analysis, the ICILS DSE model achieved configural and metric cross-country invariance, but scalar invariance could not be established due to a change in CFI (-.007) that exceeded the cut-off criterion. This allow us to compare the factor loadings across countries, but it does not permit the comparison of latent means, as different cultures may have interpreted the items diferently (i.e., the intercepts are not equivalent). Aditionaly, the multi-group model shown a significantly worst adjustment than the global model, with a RMSEA of .093. On the other hand, the model did passed all three nested levels (configural, metric and scalar) of gender invariance, with changes of the key indices within acceptable ranges.

## PISA

### Pooled model and adjustments

![](images/pisa_model.png)

The initial PISA model shown vast sources of misfit (RMSEA = .12), in particular because of two items having strong cross-loadings with the another factor and multiple residual covariances with other indicators. The first item, "Select the most efficient programme or App that allows me to carry out a specific task", shown a big charge to the general factor (mi = 76,502), and strong negative standarized residual covariance with the specialized subdimension items "logical solution" (-138.13), "identify error" (-138.24) and "programming" (-120.52). Aditionally, it had a big positive residual covariance with change settings (161.21), a item corresponding to the general DSE factor. Therefore, to maintain the parsimony of the model we removed the item. In contrast to our theorized model, the data suggest that this item has little to no relation to the programming-related tasks of the specialized dimension. The second item that shown significant problems was "Create, update and maintain a webpage or a blog", also presenting a strong cross-loading to the general factor (mi = 39,014) and big residual covariances, possitive ones with general DSE items (i.e., "collect data" (113.72), "create media" (128.92) and "change settings" (112.41)) and negative with the specialized DSE indicators (i.e., "logical solution" (-107.93) and "identify error" (-111.12)).

After re-especification, the PISA model shown a razonable fit to the data ($\chi^2$ = 37625.623; p \< .001; CFI = .994; TLI = .992; RMSEA = .068). Their factor loadings were all high, scoring between .78 and .93, and explaining among 63 and 87% of the item variance. Aditionaly, both factors had a good reliability and convergence (for General DSE: $\omega$ = .95; AVE = .71; for Specialized DSE: $\omega$ = .89; AVE = .8). The inter-factor correlation is moderate at .49.
